text:
## Recommendation

Product effort should prioritize **usability** next quarter, specifically `usability.ad_frequency` (5488 complaints [C09], severity sum 11849 [C10]) and `billing.features_locked_behind_premium` (4490 complaints [C05], severity sum 13442 [C06]). These two issues combine high volume with high severity and sit just behind the large `other.general` catch-all (14039 complaints [C01], severity sum 28433 [C02]) in overall priority_score, making them the most actionable, specific levers available this review window.

## Evidence

- **billing.features_locked_behind_premium** — 4490 complaints [C05], severity_sum 13442 [C08], mean_severity 2.993764 [C07]. Customers describe previously-free playback actions (skipping, seeking, playing searched/saved songs) now gated behind Premium. Example: "I can only 6 skip 6 stacks per hour now I can't play a song which i searched up everything is removed you need premium to do anything I am planning on switching to yt music instead of this now" [a0d2ccd3-ebb3-46b9-bbf7-212bb0ec8e84]; also "I wish I could give this app minus stars, it has started charging money for even playing the playlist normally" [33a171b5-b930-48c3-8560-97b8deb538be]. Note the first quote expresses cancellation intent, not a confirmed cancellation.

- **usability.ad_frequency** — 5488 complaints [C09], severity_sum 11849 [C12], mean_severity 2.159074 [C11]. Complaints center on excessive or disruptive ads. Example of severity: "Today I almost got into an accident because of unexpected loud ad music" [08a1f178-3e7a-4d65-9da3-dee293dd0061].

- **usability.playback_controls_limited** (rank 5) — 1592 complaints [C17], severity_sum 4797 [C20], mean_severity 3.013191 [C19], the highest mean severity among the top usability issues. Example: "The new update is so bad I can't even swith the previous song back and I can't even listen to my playlist." [9a2f9235-5c31-4726-baf5-dbb5910e345c]; also "Dude u can't even trun it back or forth why people obsessed such a bitching appa" [09a197ce-c9d5-4be6-84ef-eab81f021bd9].

- **other.general** — 14039 complaints [C01], severity_sum 28433 [C04], the single largest issue bucket, but by definition it is a catch-all with no specific, placeable defect (e.g., "It is one of the worst app as it has only work to collect users personal data only." [9fc1772d-03b5-4d0e-b48c-8aa97cef68c2]). It cannot itself guide engineering work, so it is reported but not used to set the priority area.

## Alternatives considered

At the topic level: usability has 13163 complaint/cancellation reviews and severity sum 33278 [F14, F15], the largest of any named topic. Billing has 6875 reviews and severity sum 20158 [F18, F19]. Playback has 5615 reviews and severity sum 18451 [F20, F21]. Access has only 1610 reviews and severity sum 6291 [F22, F23], substantially smaller than usability, billing, or playback — making it the lowest current priority among the four candidate areas. Support, a billing/support-adjacent topic, is very small (118 reviews, severity sum 362 [F28, F29]).

Within playback, the leading specific issue is `playback.app_crashes_freezes` (1160 complaints [C29], severity_sum 4062 [C32], mean_severity 3.501724 [C31] — the highest mean severity of any issue listed), which would justify elevation if crash volume grows or if engineering capacity opens after usability/billing fixes ship. `billing.general` (1496 complaints [C33], severity_sum 3975 [C36]) and `playback.general` (1222 complaints [C37], severity_sum 3953 [C40]) are smaller catch-alls and don't change the ranking. Access would move up in priority if its complaint_count or severity_sum rose materially above the levels reported in F22/F23, or if a specific access issue (not present in the current claims list) emerged with high severity.

## Limits

This analysis draws on a seeded random sample of review IDs [F00]; 560609 reviews [F99] were outside this classification scope, so all counts describe only the classified reviews. Of 660622 source reviews [F01], 100000 were completed classifications [F02], with 13 quarantined for empty text [F03] and 0 for other failures [F04]. 13974 completed reviews are flagged needs_review [F07] and are included in every count and ranking above; the flag marks them for human inspection, not exclusion. Verification agreement (topic 84.6% [F11], intent 91.2% [F12], severity mean absolute difference 0.155 [F13], on a 1000-review sample [F10]) reflects agreement between two models, not ground-truth accuracy. There is no revenue, plan-tier, or confirmed-churn data in this dataset; cancellation-intent reviews (4327 [F06]) reflect stated intent only, not confirmed cancellations, and no revenue or churn figures should be inferred from these counts.
